The label is textFromFloat with flags 5 (no padding): the default flags pad the number with spaces, which pushes it off centre

`size` is fixed dp and does not shrink: in a row whose width varies, spread the rings with horizontalAlignment spaceEvenly (or weighted boxes) rather than a spacedBy gap, and pick sizes that fit the narrowest host

A progress change animates: the drawing reads an animated local pa = {"value": "@progress", "anim": 0.3} (paint time). A literal progress folds to a number, so a static bar costs nothing extra; a value driven every frame just follows 0.3 s behind. Mono themes jump (the percentage label shows the true value at once)

components.name: skeleton
components.title: Skeleton
components.prompt: A loading placeholder for a list row (an avatar circle and two text lines) above an image block, with a shimmer sweeping across.
teaches: shape picks a line (text), a circle (an avatar, `height` wide) or a block (an image); width omitted fills the space
The shimmer is a linear gradient whose ends move with continuousSec(), so every skeleton sweeps on the same clock
Mono draws a static grey outline: no gradient and no motion

snippets.note: circle, 40 dp: an avatar placeholder
a 150 dp text line
a block filling the width; the band crosses it every 1.5 s

check.describe: A grey avatar circle and two grey text lines, and a wide grey block below, each with a lighter band (darker in dark) crossing it; render-later, 0.5 s on, has every band further right. Resized, the block and the lines' column keep their sizes but the block fills the width: 200 dp narrow, 450 dp wide.

components.summary: A loading placeholder: a grey line, circle or block with a light band sweeping across it every 1.5 s, standing in for text, an avatar or an image until the content arrives.
pitfalls: The sweep is a linear gradient (colour, highlight, colour) whose ends move with continuousSec(): the document repaints every frame while a skeleton is on screen, so replace it with the content as soon as it arrives
Its colours are theme colours inside the gradient (the parsers mark them as colour ids), so light and dark both work: surfaceHigh with a surface band (lighter in light, darker in dark)
Each skeleton sweeps on its own width but on the same clock, so a column of them shimmers together; the band is 240 dp wide whatever the shape
Mono has no motion and no gradient: a 1.5 dp grey outline of the shape

components.name: slider
components.title: Slider
components.prompt: A volume slider from 0 to 100 that shows its value, and a brightness slider with its own state.
teaches: Bind value to a document variable ({"value": "@volume", "max": 100}) to preset it and read it below the slider; omitted (or a number), the slider keeps its own state, starting there
showValue prints the live value at the end of the track (decimals sets the digits after the point)
Dragging is a touchExpression in absolute mode: the thumb jumps under the finger and the value stays clamped to min..max

snippets.note: bound to @volume (40), 0 to 100, value shown
showValue: textFromFloat of the live value
unbound: its own state, starting at 0.7; label is the accessibility label

check.describe: Volume shows a blue track 40% full with 40 at its end; Brightness is an amber track 70% full. A tap on a track jumps the thumb under the finger and a drag follows it, clamped at the ends (checked in the Java reference: a tap at x=150 on Volume gives 50). Resized, the tracks fill the width: at 200 dp they are shorter with the thumbs at the same fractions, at 450 dp longer.

components.summary: A horizontal slider: dragging or tapping the track sets its variable between min and max (the thumb jumps under the finger and follows it); it can show the value at its end.
pitfalls: The drag is a touchExpression in absolute mode (touchMode 6) named after the bound variable: from the slider on, "@volume" is the touch value (it starts at the variable's own value and keeps where the finger left it). Read the value AFTER the slider in the document: the parsers bind names in document order, so a text placed before it, or an expression in resources, keeps reading the starting value
touchX() is in document coordinates, so the slider measures where it sits (componentValue POS_ROOT_X into a local) and subtracts it: it works anywhere in the layout, scrolled or padded

Players that predate the T31-T33 / C49-C50 fixes (2026-10-30) map the drag wrong: the TS player read 0 for POS_ROOT_X and let every slider take every touch, and the C++ player hit-tested a nested touch expression in its own coordinates. Java, and the TS and C++ players from that date, put the value under the finger
The value is continuous: there are no steps (the notch stop modes need touchSpec, which the Java parser ignores, U8). Round where you read it (textFromFloat decimals, floor())
It fills the width it is given (fillMaxWidth) and is 40 dp tall: in a row, give it a weight or a box with a width
No easing on the value: the thumb follows the finger frame for frame (an animated value would trail it). In mono it looks the same, a thin grey track, a thicker white active part and a smaller thumb

components.name: sparkline
components.title: Sparkline
components.prompt: Show weekly visits as a small trend line next to its label, and a temperature series as a sparkline across the card.
teaches: Call {"Sparkline": {"values": "@visits"}} with the name of a float array in resources.floatArrays; export it and the host can replace the series
A fixed width × height (120 × 32 by default) sits beside a label; fill: true takes the space of a sized or weighted parent
The line spans the data's min..max and ends on a dot at the latest value

snippets.note: bound to the exported float array visits
one drawLine per pair of values, in a loop over the array
fill: true, scaled with componentWidth()/componentHeight()

check.describe: A blue rising line 120 × 32 beside 'Visits, 8 weeks', ending on a dot at 84; under it a violet line across the full width, peaking at the ninth value. With variables {visits: [84, 69, 73, 58, 61, 48, 55, 42]} the small line falls instead. At 234 and 540 dp wide the lower line stretches to the width; the small one stays 120 dp.

components.summary: A word-sized trend line: one stroke through every value of a float array, scaled from its min to its max to fill the canvas, with a dot on the latest value.
pitfalls: values is the name of a float array ("@visits" declared in resources.floatArrays), not a JSON list: the chart reads it with arrayGet in a loop, so a host that sets the exported array redraws it with no new document, and any length works
The line is a loop of drawLine segments (round caps hide the joins), not an SVG path: a path string costs about 4 KB in Java

The y range is the data's own min..max, so a flat series sits on the bottom edge and small changes look large; that is what a sparkline is for, but don't put one next to a bar chart and expect the same scale
Everything scales with componentWidth() and componentHeight(), read inline in each coordinate; it keeps the call out of pattern mode, which is fine for a chart drawn once or twice

components.name: stat-tile
components.title: StatTile
components.prompt: Show two KPI tiles side by side, revenue and latency, each with its value, unit and change since last week.
teaches: Call {"StatTile": {"label": "Revenue", "value": "@revenue", "unit": "k€", "delta": "@revenueDelta"}}: the delta's sign picks the chevron and the colour
Set invert true for metrics where lower is better (latency, churn, cost): a rise turns red
The tile fills its width: two side by side are weighted boxes with a fixed 12 dp spacer box between them

snippets.note: value and delta bound to exported variables
a rounded surface tile
invert: a positive delta is drawn red

check.describe: Two tiles: Revenue 128 k€ with a green up chevron and 4.2, Latency 182 ms with a red up chevron and 12.0; revenueDelta -3 turns the first one red with a down chevron. The tiles are weighted halves: at 234 dp they narrow and the numbers and units still fit, at 540 dp each tile widens.

components.summary: A KPI tile filling its width: a label, a live value with its unit, and an optional delta with an up chevron when positive, a down chevron otherwise, green when the change is good and red when it is bad (invert for metrics where lower is better).
pitfalls: Colour by sign without colour expressions: the delta is drawn twice, green with paint alpha @up and red with 1 - @up, where the local up is step(@delta, 0); step(x, edge) is x > edge, so 0 counts as a fall
Numbers use textFromFloat flags 5: the default flags pad the integer part with spaces (whole 6 puts four spaces before 42), which shifts the value right
The tile fills its width: put two side by side as weighted boxes with a fixed spacer box between them (weights ignore spacedBy)
abs(@delta) and step(@delta, 0) are locals, each computed once for the call (a literal delta folds both to numbers)

The label is one line with an ellipsis, so a narrow tile shortens it with … instead of wrapping it into the value. The value and unit do not shrink: a 128 k€ tile needs about 100 dp, so below that use one tile per row

components.name: stepper
components.title: Stepper
components.prompt: Add a plus / minus control to pick the number of guests, from 1 to 8.
teaches: Call {"Stepper": {"value": "@guests", "min": 1, "max": 8, "label": "guests"}}: − and + change the bound variable by `step`, clamped to [min, max]
For fractional steps give step and decimals together (step 0.5, decimals 1), and bind a variable that starts at the value you want
`label` names the quantity for accessibility ("Decrease guests"); show the same words as text beside the stepper

snippets.note: bound to guests, 1..8: the render taps + once
the buttons set min(@max, @guests + @step) and max(@min, @guests - @step)
half-kilo steps, the value printed with one decimal

check.describe: Guests reads 3 after the render's tap on + (it starts at 2); Weight, kg reads 2.5; tapping − on weight shows 2.0. The steppers keep their size at the end of each row and the labels sit in weighted boxes: at 234 dp "Weight, kg" ends in …, at 540 dp the labels keep their place and the + tap still lands.

components.summary: A minus / value / plus control that changes a number by `step`, clamped to [min, max].
pitfalls: textFromFloat `whole` is the number of integer digits kept, not a minimum: whole 1 prints 10 as 0. The value uses whole 3 with flags 5 (no padding), so it stays centred
The buttons clamp with max(@min, @value - @step) and min(@max, @value + @step): a value outside [min, max] set by the host is pulled back on the next tap
The buttons are announced as Decrease and Increase, followed by `label` when given ("Decrease guests"); put the stepper next to a KeyValueRow key that names the quantity

components.name: switch
components.title: Switch
components.prompt: Add an on/off toggle switch for Wi-Fi next to its label, like in a settings screen.
teaches: Call {"Switch": {"label": "Wi-Fi", "checked": "@wifi"}} and declare wifi (0 or 1) in resources.variables: a tap flips it, and the rest of the document can read or preset it
Leave `checked` out and the switch keeps its own state, starting off; `color` sets the track colour when on
Put the visible label beside it (a text and a weighted spacer box in a row) and pass the same words as `label`

snippets.note: a Switch bound to the document variable wifi, which starts on
unbound, with a green track: it keeps its own state (tapped on in the render)
label is the accessibility label; the visible Bluetooth text sits beside it

check.describe: Wi-Fi is on (blue), Bluetooth off (grey); the render taps Battery saver, which slides on with a green track. Switches stay at the end of their rows and the labels sit in weighted boxes: at 160 dp "Battery saver" ends in …, at 540 dp the switches move to the right edge (the tap follows them).

components.summary: An on/off switch: a tap flips its variable (0 or 1); the thumb springs across (a little overshoot) while the track colour fades in.
pitfalls: The motion is paint time: an animated local p = {"value": "@checked", "anim": 0.3} eases from 0 to 1 when the state flips (Java re-evaluates an animated expression every frame while it runs), and the thumb x is 16 + 20 * (p + 0.5 * sin(pi * p) * (2 * @checked - 1)): the sine term pushes it about 10% past the end and back, the spring feel. No layout runs while it moves
The track colour follows the state without colour expressions: the `color` track is drawn over the grey one with paint alpha p
Mono themes have no motion: p is @checked itself, so the thumb and the track snap (the sine term is 0 at both ends)
It draws no text: put the visible label next to it (a KeyValueRow key, a ListItem title) and pass the same words as `label`

components.name: tabs
components.title: Tabs
components.prompt: Add a Day / Week / Month tab bar whose selected tab is highlighted with an underline.
teaches: Call {"Tabs": {"labels": ["Day", "Week", "Month"], "selected": "@tab"}}: the labels are static, a tap sets tab to the tab's index
Bind a document variable (tab, 0 here) so panels and PagerDots can follow the selection; a tap on a tab sets it to that tab's index
Panels below follow the same variable (graphicsLayer alpha 1 - min(1, abs(@tab - i))); the bar does not switch content itself

snippets.note: three tabs bound to the document variable tab (the render taps Week)
equal-width tabs: each is a weight 1 box
each label is also its tab's accessibility label

check.describe: The render taps Week: it lights up in blue with the underline under it; Day and Month are muted. The tabs share the width by weight and the underline is a fraction of componentWidth(): at 234 and 540 dp the middle tap still selects Week and the underline sits under it.

components.summary: A 48 dp tab bar of equal-width tabs from a static list of labels: a tap sets `selected` to the tab's index; the underline slides to the tapped tab while the labels cross-fade to `color`.
pitfalls: labels is static: the tabs are generated when the document is built ($each), and their number is the local n ({"$count": "labels"}); the selection is the runtime part

The motion is an animated local s = {"value": "@selected", "anim": 0.25}: it eases to the new index at paint time, and everything visible reads s, not @selected (the tap still sets @selected at once, so panels can switch immediately)
Each tab's highlight is a second, coloured copy of its label over the muted one, with graphicsLayer alpha 1 - min(1, abs(s - i)): 1 on the selected tab, 0 elsewhere, a cross-fade while s moves
The underline is one 2 dp canvas under the row: a rect from s * componentWidth() / n to (s + 1) * componentWidth() / n, so it slides between tabs
Mono themes have no motion: s is @selected, the underline and the highlight jump
Show the matching panel with the same alpha expression on stacked panels (or visibility); the tab bar does not switch content by itself

components.name: top-bar
components.title: TopBar
components.prompt: Put an app bar at the top of the screen with a back arrow, the title Settings and a search button on the right.
teaches: Call {"TopBar": {"title": "Inbox"}} for a 56 dp bar that fills the width, on @colors.surface
Put a back or menu icon button in slots.navigation and icon buttons in slots.actions: the actions are pushed to the end
Make each icon button a 40 dp clipped box with a ripple, a semantics contentDescription and an onClick, around a 20 dp canvas icon

snippets.note: the default call: a title only
a labelled 40 dp back button, centred icon
a search action, pushed to the end by the bar's weighted spacer

check.describe: Two bars: Inbox alone, and Settings with a back arrow before the title and a magnifier at the right end; tapping them sets action to 1 and 2. The bars fill the width: at 160 dp "Settings" ends in … and the search action stays on screen, at 540 dp the action moves to the end.

components.summary: An app bar: optional navigation content, a title, and actions pushed to the end.
pitfalls: The title sits in the weighted box (weight 1; the text is one line with an ellipsis): it pushes the actions to the end and, in a narrow bar, shortens with … instead of pushing them off the edge. Weight the box, not the text: the C++ player gives a weighted text its full width and squeezes the actions to nothing. The bar is 56 dp tall and fills its width
Icon buttons in the slots need their own semantics contentDescription and a 40 to 48 dp box: a bare canvas is neither labelled nor easy to hit

components.name: weather-icon
components.title: Weather icon
components.prompt: Draw weather symbols for sunny, cloudy, rain, snow and thunderstorm, without images or SVG paths, labelled underneath.
teaches: {"WeatherIcon": {"condition": "rain"}} draws a 48 dp symbol; condition is static (sun, cloud, rain, snow, storm) and size scales the 24-unit drawing
A cloud is three circles over a rounded rectangle; the mono outline is the same shapes drawn larger in onSurface and then in the background colour, which outlines their union
Sun rays are one line in a loop that rotates the canvas 45° per pass, so the paint is set once

snippets.note: sun: disc and eight rays from a rotate loop
rain: cloud of circles and a rounded rect, three slanted lines
storm at 32 dp with its own label

check.describe: Five distinct 48 dp icons in equal columns, each labelled: an amber sun with eight rays, a grey cloud centred in its square, a cloud over three slanted blue drops, a cloud over three blue dots, and a cloud over an amber bolt; below, a 32 dp storm icon. In mono the sun is a ring with rays and the clouds are white outlines. The columns are weighted: at 260 dp they get closer, at 480 dp they spread out; the icons keep their size.

components.summary: A square weather symbol drawn with circles, rounded rectangles and lines: sun, cloud, rain, snow or storm.
pitfalls: condition is static: each condition is a different drawing written into the document. To show a condition the host chooses at run time, put the five icons in a stateLayout (or behind visibility) driven by a host integer
No SVG paths: the cloud is three circles over a rounded rectangle, and the bolt three round-capped lines (an SVG path string costs about 4 KB in Java, padded to 1024 floats)

Mono draws the cloud as an outline: the same shapes 1.25 units larger in onSurface, then the shapes themselves in @colors.background, so the ring follows their union. It assumes the icon sits on the background colour, which every surface is in mono
The sun's eight rays are one line drawn in a loop that rotates the canvas 45° per pass (8 × 45° = 360°, back to the start)
